source_text: Ὡς δὲ καὶ λήσειν ἔμελλε τοὺς ἄλλους ἀνθρώπους γεννηθεὶς ὁ Χριστὸς ἄχρις ἀνδρωθῇ. ὅπερ καὶ γέγονεν, ἀκούσατε τῶν προειρημένων εἰς τοῦτο. Ἔστι δὲ ταῦτα· „Παιδίον ἐγεννήθη ἡμῖν, καὶ νεανίσκος ἡμῖν ἀπεδόθη, οὗ ἡ ἀρχ(??) ἐπὶ τῶν ὤμων“· μηνυτικὸν τῆς δυνάμεως τοῦ σταυροῦ, ᾧ προσέθηκε τοὺς ὤμους σταυρωθείς, ὡς πρωϊόντος τοῦ λόγον σαφέστερον δειχθήσεται. Καὶ πάλιν ὁ αὐτὸς προφήτης Ἡσαΐας θεοφορούμενος τῷ πνεύματι τῷ προφητικῷ ἔφη· ,Ἐγώ ἐξεπέτασα τὰς χεῖράς μου ἐπὶ λαὸν ἀπειθοῦντα καὶ ἀντιλέγοντα, ἐπὶ τοὺς πορευομένους ἐν ὁδῷ οὐ καλῇ. Αἰτοῦσί με νῦν κρίσιν καὶ ἐγγίζειν θεῷ τολμῶσιν“. Καὶ πάλιν ἐν ἄλλοις λόγοις δι᾿ ἑτέρου προφήτου λέγει· „Αὐιοὶ ὤρυξάν μου πόδας καὶ χεῖρας, καὶ ἔβαλον κλῆρον ἐπὶ τὸν ἱματισμόν μου“. Καὶ ὁ μὲν Δαυῒδ ὁ βασιλεὺς καὶ προφήτης, ὁ εἰπὼν ταῦτα, οὐδὲν τούτων ἔπαθεν· Ἰησοῦς δὲ Χριστὸς ἐξετάθη τὰς χεῖρας, σταυρωθεὶς ὑπὸ τῶν Ἰουδαίων ἀντιλεγόντων αὐτῷ καὶ φασκόντων μὴ εἶναι αὐτὸν Χριστόν· καὶ γάρ, ὡς εἶπεν ὁ προφήτης, διασύροντες αὐτὸν ἐκάθισαν ἐπὶ βήματος καὶ εἶπον· Κρῖνον ἡμῖν. Τὸ δὲ „Ὤρυξάν μου χεῖρας καὶ πόδας‘· ἐξήγησις τῶν ἐν τῷ σταυρῷ παγέντων ἐν ταῖς χερσὶ καὶ τοῖς ποσὶν αὐτοῦ ἥλων ἦν. Καὶ μετὰ τὸ σταυρῶσαι αὐτὸν ἔβαλον κλῆρον ἐπὶ τὸν ἱματισμὸν αὐτοῦ καὶ ἐμερίσαντο ἑαυτοῖς οἱ σταυρώσαντες αὐτόν. Καὶ ταῦτα ὅτι γέγονε, δύνασθε μαθεῖν ἐκ τῶν ἐπὶ Ποντίου Πιλάτου γενομένων ἄκτων. Καὶ ὅτι ῥητῶς καθεσθησόμενος ἐπὶ πῶλον ὄνου καὶ εἰσελευσόμενος εἰς τὰ Ἱεροσόλυμα προεπεφήτευτο, ἑτέρου προφήτου τοῦ Σοφονίου τας τῆς προφητείας λέξεις ἐροῦμεν. Εἰσὶ δὲ αὗται· „Χαῖρε σφόδρα, θύγατερ Σιών, κήρυσσε, θύγατερ Ἱερουσαλήμ· ἰδοὺ ὁ βασιλεύς σου ἔρχεται σοι πρᾶος, ἐπιβεβηκὼς ἐπὶ ὄνον καὶ πῶλον υἱὸν ὑποζυγίου“.
pass_a_gloss: As also He was about to release the other men being born the Christ until He becomes a man, which also happened, hear the previously mentioned things to this effect: For there is (as Isaiah said) "A child has been born to us, and a young man has been given to us, whose authority is upon the shoulders" (Isaiah 9:6), a sign of the power of the cross, to which He drew near having been crucified, putting His shoulders to it, as will be shown more clearly in the morning of the word. And again the same prophet Isaiah, being borne by the prophetic Spirit, said: "I stretched out my hands to a disobedient and contradicting people, to those walking in a way not good" (Isaiah 65:2). They ask me now for judgment and dare to draw near to God. And again in other words through another prophet He says: "They pierced my hands and feet, and cast lots for my clothing" (Psalm 22:16). And King David, the prophet who said these things, did not suffer any of these things; but Jesus Christ was examined, having His hands pierced, being crucified by the Jews who contradicted Him and said He was not the Christ; and indeed, as the prophet said, they dragged Him away, sat Him on a judgment seat, and said: Judge us. The "They pierced my hands and feet" is an explanation of the things happening on the cross, the nails in His hands and feet. And after they crucified Him, they cast lots for His clothing and divided it among themselves, those who crucified Him. And that these things happened, you are able to learn from the acts that took place under Pontius Pilate. And that having been explicitly set upon a foal of a donkey and entering into Jerusalem was prophesied, we will say the words of the prophecy of another prophet, Zechariah: "Rejoice greatly, daughter of Zion, proclaim, daughter of Jerusalem: behold your king comes to you, gentle, mounted upon a donkey and a foal, the son of a beast of burden" (Zechariah 9:9).

choices.why: indicating the purpose of Christ's birth

pass_b_english: Christ was born so that He might grow to manhood and thus free the rest of humanity; this has come to pass, so hear the words spoken beforehand to this effect (Isaiah 9:6): "A child has been born to us, and a young man has been given to us, whose authority rests upon his shoulders." This is a sign of the power of the cross, to which He drew near when He was crucified, putting His shoulders to it; the truth of this will be shown more clearly as the Word advances. And again the same prophet Isaiah, carried by the prophetic Spirit, said (Isaiah 65:2): "I stretched out my hands to a disobedient and contradicting people, to those walking in a way that is not good. They ask me now for judgment and dare to draw near to God." And again, in other words through another prophet, He says (Psalm 22:16): "They pierced my hands and feet, and cast lots for my clothing." King David, the prophet who spoke these words, did not suffer any of these things; but Jesus Christ was examined, His hands pierced, crucified by the Jews who contradicted Him and claimed He was not the Christ. And indeed, as the prophet said, they dragged Him away, sat Him on a judgment seat, and said: "Judge us." The words "They pierced my hands and feet" explain what happened on the cross—the nails driven through His hands and feet. And after they crucified Him, they cast lots for His clothing and divided it among themselves, the ones who crucified Him. You are able to learn that these things happened from the acts that took place under Pontius Pilate. And that it was explicitly prophesied that He would mount a donkey's foal and enter Jerusalem, we will speak the words of the prophecy of another prophet, Zechariah (Zechariah 9:9): "Rejoice greatly, daughter of Zion; proclaim it, daughter of Jerusalem: behold, your king comes to you, gentle, mounted upon a donkey and a foal, the son of a beast of burden."

review.notes: The translation accurately captures the Greek text, including the difficult opening clause regarding Christ's growth to manhood and the subsequent prophetic citations. Scripture citations (Isaiah 9:6, Isaiah 65:2, Psalm 22:16, Zechariah 9:9) are correctly applied to the quoted/alluded text. Pass B maintains the nuances of Pass A and the Greek source.
